Record date: 2128-11-12
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 11/12/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of renal function, and assessment of mental health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately four weeks after his last visit. He reports that his respiratory symptoms remain stable; however, he has experienced an increase in exertional dyspnea, particularly during activities like walking uphill or engaging in household chores. He continues to use his albuterol inhaler, now averaging four times daily, as he feels it provides temporary relief. The cough remains productive with clear sputum, and he denies any hemoptysis or recent respiratory infections.
He expresses concern regarding the persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, which he describes as worsening over the past week. Mr. Fairfax reports that despite adherence to dietary sodium restrictions, he has noted a weight gain of 2 pounds since the last visit, attributing this to increased fluid retention. He rates the discomfort from the edema as 7/10.
In terms of mental health, Mr. Fairfax indicates that he has been experiencing increased anxiety, particularly related to his health status and the recent changes in his physical condition. Although he continues cognitive-behavioral therapy, he reports that sleep disturbances have worsened, with difficulty falling asleep and frequent awakenings throughout the night.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + increased dyspnea on exertion, + productive cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + worsening bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using four times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 160 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 78, BP 132/82, RR 20, O2 sat 84% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.2, Hgb 10.4, Hct 30.8, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 134, K 4.4, Cl 99, CO2 22, BUN 45, Cr 2.6, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 700 (elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status has shown some deterioration with increased exertional dyspnea. An updated pulmonary function test is scheduled for next week to assess lung function. Consideration for a change in bronchodilator therapy may be warranted if symptoms persist. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. The serum creatinine has increased slightly, indicating worsening renal function. Close monitoring will be necessary, and nephrology will be consulted for further evaluation. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema has worsened despite diuretic therapy. Increase furosemide to 200 mg daily and reinforce dietary sodium restrictions. Daily weight monitoring is critical, and nephrology follow-up will be pursued. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. Referral to psychiatry for medication management is warranted due to increased anxiety and insomnia. Continued engagement in cognitive-behavioral therapy is encouraged.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
